input.reply:
Mara, here are your two approaches side by side. Right now you have ₱9,050.00 left each month after spending and minimum payments. Your idea and Jun's can't both get all of that, so the two of you need to pick one.

A, your way (clear the card fast): the whole ₱9,050.00 goes to the credit card. The card is paid off in 9 months, with ₱12,460.10 in interest. Nothing goes to the emergency fund during that time.

B, Jun's way: ₱4,000.00 extra goes to the card and ₱5,050.00 to the emergency fund. The card is paid off in 17 months, with ₱24,303.62 in interest. The fund reaches its ₱210,000.00 target in 12 months.

What to weigh: the card charges 3% a month, the most of any of your debts, so paying it fast saves the most interest. That fits your avalanche preference. But the emergency fund only covers 2.1 months of essential spending, against your 3-month target. And in August you both chose a bigger cash buffer over paying the car loan early. Option B keeps to that choice. I haven't recommended either one, because you and Jun want different things. Once the card is paid off under A, the ₱9,050.00 is free for the fund.
